This BREAKS the new delivery-pin feature end-to-end for customers.

critical.issue: Returns 422 'Field required: body.user_id' when frontend AddressManagement.js posts formData (which does not include user_id). Server code overrides user_id from current_user AFTER Pydantic validation, so the endpoint is unusable from the UI. This blocks the new Delivery Pin feature (customer cannot save an address). Fix: create AddressCreate BaseModel (like ClaimCreate) without user_id, or make user_id Optional in Address model.

Once main agent creates an AddressCreate body model (mirroring ClaimCreate), retest Delivery Pin persistence: create address with lat/lng → GET /api/addresses shows lat/lng → re-open Edit modal shows pin at saved location.
rca of the issue: Root cause: server.py:3215 uses `address: Address` as the request-body model. The Address model in models.py:407 declares `user_id: str` (required). The frontend AddressManagement.js:114 posts formData that omits user_id (relying on the server to set it from the session). Pydantic v2 rejects the payload with 422 BEFORE the endpoint body runs, so line 3219 `address.user_id = current_user.id` never executes. Reproduction: `curl -X POST /api/addresses -H 'Authorization: Bearer <cust-jwt>' -d '{...no user_id...}'` → 422 missing field. Mitigation: create `class AddressCreate(BaseModel)` with the same fields minus user_id (analogous to ClaimCreate at server.py:3492), change the endpoint signature to `payload: AddressCreate`, and construct the Address inside the handler with `user_id=current_user.id`. Apply the same fix to PUT /api/addresses/{id} if it uses the same pattern.
